found.family: web (educational and synthetic web text, plus topic labels for weighting computer-science pages)

datasets.name: FineWeb-Edu (int_score >= 3, the default set)
datasets.size: 1.3T GPT-2 tokens per the card (that figure dates from v1.0; later versions added dumps, and the card does not give an updated total). 1.53B rows. Per-dump configs plus samples: sample-10BT (9.67M rows), sample-100BT (97.3M rows), sample-350BT (339M rows). Our 16k tokenizer (~4 letters per piece) would give somewhat more pieces than GPT-2 tokens. That is an estimate, not measured.
datasets.licence: ODC-By (plus Common Crawl terms of use)
datasets.version_date: v1.4.0, 11 July 2025 (CC-MAIN-2013-20 to CC-MAIN-2025-26). v1.3.0 31 Jan 2025 (+~35B tokens of fixed dumps). v1.2.0 3 Jan 2025. v1.0.0 2 June 2024.
datasets.quality_notes: Llama3-70B-Instruct rated 500k FineWeb pages 0-5. A Snowflake-arctic-embed regression classifier was trained on them (F1 82% at threshold 3), and keeping >= 3 removed ~92% of FineWeb. Columns: score (float, 2.52-5.06), int_score (3-5), language_score, token_count (GPT-2). The default set is NOT deduplicated across dumps. The authors report dedup made no difference in their ablation (1.8B model, 350B tokens). Strong on MMLU/ARC/OpenBookQA and weaker on HellaSwag/PIQA/CommonsenseQA. The card notes thresholds above 3 help knowledge and reasoning but hurt HellaSwag/PIQA. int_score is rounded, so >=3 really means a raw score of about 2.5 or more. A third-party card (NMAIResearch, unverified) says 57% of kept pages got in by rounding.
datasets.recommended_subset: Prefer the deduplicated SmolLM-Corpus copy (next entry) as the base. To weight up the best pages, take int_score >= 4 (or raw score >= 3.5) from the newest dumps (2024-2025, not in the dedup copy) and give it about 2x weight. The token size of the >= 4 slice is unconfirmed; it can be computed by summing token_count where int_score >= 4. FineWeb-Edu is far larger than our needs (35% of 80B = 28B pieces, well under one pass).
datasets.used_by: SmolLM2-1.7B: 60% FineWeb-Edu / 40% DCLM web blend in stage 1 (0-6T tokens), shifting toward DCLM later (stage 4: 58% English web at a higher DCLM ratio). SmolLM3-3B: part of 85% web in stage 1 (with DCLM, FineWeb2, FineWeb2-HQ). Exact per-source shares unconfirmed.

datasets.name: FineWeb-Edu-dedup (SmolLM-Corpus)
datasets.size: 220B GPT-2 tokens, 190M rows. The whole SmolLM-Corpus is 673 GB of files (cosmopedia-v2 + fineweb-edu-dedup + python-edu); the GB of the dedup part alone is unconfirmed.
datasets.licence: ODC-By
datasets.version_date: July 2024 (SmolLM release); built from the FineWeb-Edu dumps available then (exact dump range unconfirmed)
datasets.quality_notes: Deduplicated across dumps (the card just says "deduplicated"; the method is not detailed on the page). 220B GPT-2 tokens is about 8x what a 35% share of 80B pieces needs, so no repetition is needed.
datasets.recommended_subset: Use as the main FineWeb-Edu source. Keep score/int_score if present for weighting (column presence on this config unconfirmed). Top up with int_score >= 4 pages from FineWeb-Edu v1.2-1.4 dumps (2024-2025) for recency.
datasets.used_by: SmolLM (v1, 135M/360M/1.7B, July 2024) pretraining corpus; share unconfirmed.

datasets.name: FineWeb-Edu-score-2 (int_score >= 2)
datasets.size: About 5.4T GPT-2 tokens (FineWeb-Edu card and FineWeb blog)
datasets.licence: ODC-By
datasets.quality_notes: Threshold 2 scored below threshold 3 but above plain FineWeb in the authors' ablations. Not needed at 80B; listed only as the pool for a DCLM-like broader-style fraction if DCLM is not used.
datasets.recommended_subset: Not recommended (FineWeb-Edu >= 3 plus DCLM-Edu covers it).
datasets.used_by: none known among the small-model reports checked

datasets.name: DCLM-Baseline 1.0
datasets.size: About 4T tokens on the card, about 3.8T in the paper (GPT-NeoX tokenizer per secondary summaries; tokenizer not stated on the card). ~3B documents, ~7.2 TB of files.
datasets.licence: CC-BY-4.0. The card notes intended use for research; read the card before commercial use.
datasets.quality_notes: RefinedWeb-style heuristics, Bloom-filter dedup, then a fastText classifier trained on OpenHermes 2.5 and r/ExplainLikeImFive. This favours Q&A- and explanation-style text, which suits chat. The card says it is weak on code and maths. In the SmolLM2 ablations (350B tokens) it beat FineWeb-Edu on HellaSwag (62.3 vs 60.1), CommonsenseQA (40.1 vs 36.2) and PIQA (76.9 vs 76.2), and lost on MMLU (35.5 vs 37.5), ARC (53.5 vs 57.5) and OpenBookQA (40.8 vs 41.9). The 60/40 FineWeb-Edu/DCLM blend kept most of both.
datasets.recommended_subset: Do not take raw DCLM. Use DCLM-Edu (next entry), the variant SmolLM2 used at 135M/360M.
datasets.used_by: OLMo 2 (olmo-mix-1124 is mostly DCLM-Baseline, ~3.7T of ~3.9T tokens; Dolmino mid-training used a filtered DCLM high-quality subset); SmolLM2-1.7B (40% of web in stage 1); SmolLM3 (part of web).

datasets.name: DCLM-Edu (DCLM re-filtered with the FineWeb-Edu classifier)
datasets.size: About 1.0B rows (estimated by the viewer), 5.13 TB of files. Token count and tokenizer not stated on the card (unconfirmed).
datasets.licence: CC-BY-4.0 (follows DCLM-Baseline)
datasets.version_date: No release date on the card; linked to the SmolLM2 paper (4 Feb 2025)
datasets.quality_notes: Keeps DCLM pages with FineWeb-Edu score > 2. The card itself says keeping only edu_int_score >= 3 gave better results for small models. The SmolLM2 paper describes the 135M/360M web data as DCLM with score-0 pages removed and scores 1-2 downsampled. It combines DCLM's conversational/Q&A style with educational filtering.
datasets.recommended_subset: edu_int_score >= 3 only. Suggested split of the web share: about 60% FineWeb-Edu(-dedup) / 40% DCLM-Edu >= 3, following SmolLM2's 60/40 blend. In the final decay phase, shift toward the >= 4 slices of both.
datasets.used_by: SmolLM2-135M (2T tokens) and SmolLM2-360M (4T tokens), the closest strong models to 560M; exact share unconfirmed (single-stage run with Stack-Edu, InfiWebMath, FineMath and Cosmopedia included from the start).

datasets.name: Ultra-FineWeb (English)
datasets.size: English about 1T tokens per the card and the paper's conclusion (the abstract says ~1.1T; tokenizer for the count unconfirmed: the paper names DeepSeek-V2 for preprocessing and MiniCPM3-4B for training). 1.16B English rows; 10.2 TB total including the Chinese part.
datasets.licence: Apache 2.0 on the card, which also says to respect the source datasets' licences (FineWeb is ODC-By)
datasets.version_date: Paper 9 May 2025; data released 6 June 2025 with MiniCPM4; card says Ultra-FineWeb-L1 released 20 Aug 2026, with the current set (L2 layer) covering Common Crawl up to CC-MAIN-2025-51
datasets.quality_notes: Built from FineWeb with a verification-based fastText classifier (threshold 0.5). At 1B parameters / 100B tokens: English average 45.89 vs FineWeb-Edu 44.56 vs FineWeb 42.28; MMLU 32.24 vs 31.80; ARC-C 35.67 vs 34.56. That is a small gain over FineWeb-Edu and overlaps heavily with it (same FineWeb source). Note that ablations were run with another lab's tokenizer and model.
datasets.recommended_subset: Optional. Either use it as a drop-in for part of the FineWeb-Edu share, or skip it. The overlap with FineWeb-Edu is high and the gain is about +1.3 points. Do not stack it on top of FineWeb-Edu without dedup between them.

datasets.name: Nemotron-CC (v1): high-quality real + synthetic (Diverse QA, Distill, Extract Knowledge, Knowledge List, Wikipedia-style rephrase)
datasets.size: 6.3T tokens in total: 4.4T globally deduplicated real + 1.9T synthetic. Real by quality: High 553B (12.6%), Medium-High 504B, Medium 2,023B, Medium-Low 894B, Low 402B. Synthetic: ~1.5T from high-quality pages (5 prompts) and 336.3B Wikipedia-style rephrasings of low-quality pages. The Nemotron-CC-HQ subset is 1.1T (0.6T real + 0.5T synthetic). Tokenizer for the counts is not stated in the paper (unconfirmed).
datasets.licence: Common Crawl Terms of Use (data); NeMo Curator code Apache 2.0
datasets.quality_notes: Strongest published web-quality result. At 8B parameters / 1T tokens, MMLU: Nemotron-CC-HQ 59.0 vs DCLM 53.4 vs FineWeb-Edu 42.9. That is at a much bigger model and budget, and it partly reflects MMLU-shaped synthetic QA. The Diverse QA synthetic text restates page facts as yes/no, multiple-choice and open questions. That directly serves the 'facts in varied wordings' requirement, but it is LLM-written (Mistral-NeMo-12B), so mistakes in it are possible. Replacing 4 of 8 high-quality repetitions with synthetic rephrasings raised the average from 55.8 to 56.7.
datasets.recommended_subset: High bucket real text plus the high-quality Diverse QA / Distill synthetic files. A few billion pieces (for example 3-6% of 80B) as a 'varied wording' fact source alongside Cosmopedia. Check which files hold which bucket before downloading (layout unconfirmed).
datasets.used_by: NVIDIA 8B trained on 15T tokens with 7.2T from Nemotron-CC (reported better than Llama 3.1 8B); later Nemotron models. Small-model shares unconfirmed.

datasets.name: Nemotron-CC-v2 (and the wider Nemotron pretraining collection)
datasets.size: Per-subset sizes not shown on the card (unconfirmed). The collection table: English Common Crawl 3,359.8B, English Synthetic CC 1,257.3B, Diverse QA 692.9B, Translated Diverse QA 558.2B, plus maths/code/SFT parts (total 6,585.8B). Tokenizer not stated.
datasets.licence: NVIDIA Data Agreement for Model Training (gated; model training only). The card says trained models may also fall under Qwen and DeepSeek licence terms, because Qwen3-30B-A3B wrote part of the synthetic text.
datasets.version_date: v1.0, 18 Aug 2025 (adds eight 2024-2025 Common Crawl snapshots)
datasets.quality_notes: Same pipeline as v1 with newer crawls. Synthetic text by Mistral-NeMo-12B (1,629.1B) and Qwen3-30B-A3B (879.1B). The licence is more restrictive than v1's.
datasets.recommended_subset: Prefer v1 (Common Crawl terms, no gate) unless 2024-2025 recency is wanted. If v2 is used, the owner must accept the gated agreement himself and check the inherited Qwen/DeepSeek terms.

datasets.name: Cosmopedia v2 (SmolLM-Corpus)
datasets.hf_id_or_url: https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceTB/smollm-corpus (config cosmopedia-v2; the cosmopedia-v2 URL redirects here)
datasets.size: 28B tokens (SmolLM blog; tokenizer for that figure not stated; per-row token_length uses the Mistral-7B tokenizer per the card). 39.1M documents.
datasets.licence: ODC-By
datasets.quality_notes: Written by Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct from over 34,000 topics. Topics come from a BISAC book-classification list: 5,000 topics in 51 categories, some expanded into subtopics by Mixtral. Each prompt is seeded with web pages retrieved from FineWeb CC-MAIN-2024-10 and 2023-50 (1,000 per topic, 34M seeds). Audience: 40% middle school, 30% college, 30% other (including v1 stories and Stanford-course textbooks). Includes ~1B tokens of Python code textbooks (seeds from AutoMathText). Columns: prompt, text, token_length, audience (10 classes), format (15), seed_data (9). Middle-school textbooks scored best on every benchmark except MMLU. Dedup and benchmark-decontamination steps are not described (unconfirmed). It is synthetic, so factual errors from Mixtral are possible, and it has a uniform style.
datasets.recommended_subset: Can supply 15% (12B pieces, under one pass at ~28B tokens), but consider 8-12% and moving the rest to DCLM-Edu / Nemotron Diverse QA for more variety. Filter by audience/format to weight up college-level and CS/maths topics. Cosmopedia v2 is the natural pick for computer-basics explanations (BISAC 'Computers' category; per-category sizes unconfirmed). Drop or cap the story format if conversation data covers storytelling.
datasets.used_by: SmolLM (v1) pretraining; SmolLM2-135M/360M from the start (share unconfirmed); SmolLM2-1.7B stage 4 decay at 4%. Also 15% of SmolLM2's tokenizer training mix.

datasets.name: Essential-Web v1.0 (with EAI taxonomy labels)
datasets.size: About 24T tokens, 23.6B documents, 75.3 TB (tokenizer for the count unconfirmed). Paper subsets: STEM 1.74T (0.91T with the DCLM filter); web code 145B (564B with DCLM); medical 433B; maths 29B.
datasets.licence: ODC-By (plus Common Crawl terms)
datasets.quality_notes: 101 Common Crawl snapshots, deduplicated. Every page is labelled by EAI-Distill-0.5b with: FDC subject codes (Dewey-like, 3 levels), Bloom knowledge domain and cognitive process, document type v1/v2, extraction artifacts, missing content, education level, reasoning depth and technical correctness. For computer science: FDC 004/005 (Computer Science, Software Engineering) alone kept 7.5% of the data and recalled 96.5% of vetted code pages. 2.3B models trained on 320B tokens: MMLU-CS 47.0 for 'code w/ DCLM' vs 32.0 for DCLM-baseline. MMLU-STEM 34.5 for 'STEM w/ DCLM' vs 27.7 DCLM vs 26.7 FineWeb-Edu.
datasets.recommended_subset: Best source for the computer-science knowledge share. Filter FDC 004/005 AND document type in {Reference/Encyclopedic/Educational, Code/Software, Social/Forum}, plus high education level and reasoning depth, then the DCLM fastText threshold. A few billion pieces fills most of the 6% CS-knowledge slot with real web text (exact filter thresholds are in the paper's algorithms; not read here).
datasets.used_by: Essential AI's own ablations; adoption by small open models unconfirmed

datasets.name: WebOrganizer (TopicClassifier / FormatClassifier and Corpus-200B)
datasets.hf_id_or_url: https://huggingface.co/WebOrganizer (models WebOrganizer/TopicClassifier, FormatClassifier, and -NoURL variants; dataset WebOrganizer/Corpus-200B)
datasets.size: Corpus-200B: about 200B GPT-NeoX tokens, ~218M rows, ~430 GB (DCLM 1b-1x pool after RefinedWeb filters and BFF dedup). Annotation sets: 100k pages labelled by Llama-3.1-405B (295 MB), plus 8B-labelled sets.
datasets.licence: Not shown on the HF pages (unconfirmed); check github.com/CodeCreator/WebOrganizer
datasets.quality_notes: 24 topics: Adult, Art & Design, Crime & Law, Education & Jobs, Entertainment, Fashion & Beauty, Finance & Business, Food & Dining, Games, Hardware, Health, History, Home & Hobbies, Industrial, Literature, Politics, Religion, Science & Technology, Social Life, Software, Software Development, Sports & Fitness, Transportation, Travel. 24 formats include Tutorial, Knowledge Article, Academic Writing, Q&A Forum, Documentation, FAQ. Corpus-200B ships with topic and format labels, DCLM-fastText and FineWeb-Edu scores and k-means clusters. Topic x Format reweighting plus the FineWeb-Edu filter raised the average from 54.2 to 56.2 (1B models). Both quality filters already lean toward Politics, Health, Science & Technology and History, and toward Knowledge Articles, Tutorials, Academic Writing and Q&A Forums.
datasets.recommended_subset: Run TopicClassifier (small, gte-base-sized: size unconfirmed) over the chosen FineWeb-Edu/DCLM-Edu shards on the server. Weight up Software Development, Software, Hardware and Science & Technology (for example 2x) and the Tutorial/Documentation/Q&A Forum formats; cap Entertainment/Games/Fashion. This is cheaper than a separate CS dataset for the web part.
datasets.used_by: OLMo 3 / Dolma 3: topic buckets from WebOrganizer (distilled into fastText) combined with quality buckets and swarm-optimised mixing. Secondary sources; primary report arXiv 2512.13961 not read, so details unconfirmed.

datasets.name: FineFineWeb (67 domain labels on FineWeb)
datasets.size: About 4.4T tokens, 6.54B samples in total (tokenizer not stated); computer_science_and_technology domain ~203.16B tokens, ~297M samples
datasets.licence: Apache-2.0 (FineWeb source is ODC-By)
datasets.quality_notes: Domains assigned by GPT-4 URL labels, then Qwen2-7B fastText recall and Qwen2-72B BERT recall over 3 rounds. Not educational-quality filtered on its own, so it should be crossed with FineWeb-Edu scores.
datasets.recommended_subset: Alternative CS-page source: computer_science_and_technology intersected with FineWeb-Edu int_score >= 3. Lower priority than the Essential-Web taxonomy, whose CS gains are measured.

datasets.name: FinePDFs-Edu (English)
datasets.size: 350B+ tokens across 69 languages (README); English part 23M rows; English token count unconfirmed. Parent FinePDFs about 3T tokens.
datasets.licence: ODC-By
datasets.quality_notes: Educational-filtered PDF text (per-language edu classifiers). Documents are long (sample token_count up to 13k+), so it suits the 16,384-window long phase. Belongs mainly to the books/papers family; listed here as the web-derived long-document option.
datasets.recommended_subset: English edu documents of 4k-16k+ tokens, for part of the ~2B-piece long-context phase.
datasets.used_by: unconfirmed (SmolLM3 found long-data upsampling gave no extra RULER/HELMET gains)

lessons: Blend two web styles instead of picking one. In the SmolLM2 350B-token ablations, FineWeb-Edu won the knowledge benchmarks (MMLU 37.5 vs 35.5, ARC 57.5 vs 53.5) and DCLM won the common-sense/conversational ones (HellaSwag 62.3 vs 60.1, CSQA 40.1 vs 36.2). A 60/40 FineWeb-Edu/DCLM blend kept most of both (MMLU 37.0, HellaSwag 62.2). For our 35% web share, that is about 21% FineWeb-Edu + 14% DCLM-Edu (>= 3).

The closest strong models to 560M (SmolLM2-135M/360M) used DCLM re-scored with the FineWeb-Edu classifier: score 0 dropped, scores 1-2 downsampled. They also had Cosmopedia, Stack-Edu and FineMath/InfiWebMath from the start, in one stage with a 20% WSD decay. The DCLM-Edu card says keeping edu_int_score >= 3 was better for small models.

Supply is not the limit: FineWeb-Edu-dedup alone is 220B GPT-2 tokens against ~28B pieces needed, so the web share can stay at one pass or less. Spend the repetition budget (up to ~4 passes, Muennighoff 2023, a threshold SmolLM2 also targeted) on the small high-value sets: FineWeb-Edu >= 4, the CS-filtered pages, Nemotron Diverse QA, in the final decay.

A stricter educational threshold trades general text for knowledge. The FineWeb-Edu card says thresholds above 3 help knowledge/reasoning benchmarks but hurt HellaSwag/PIQA. Weight >= 4 up (e.g. 2x) rather than filtering to >= 4 only, and push the top slices hardest in the last ~10-20% (SmolLM2 and SmolLM3 both raise the high-quality and code/maths shares in the decay: SmolLM3 63% web / 24% code / 13% maths at the end).

Computer-science pages should be weighted up by subject, and there is measured evidence it works. Essential-Web's FDC 004/005 (CS, software engineering) filter plus the DCLM threshold gave MMLU-CS 47.0 vs 32.0 for DCLM-baseline (2.3B models, 320B tokens), and its STEM filter gave MMLU-STEM 34.5 vs 26.7 for FineWeb-Edu. Cheapest path: take the ready labels on Essential-Web, or run WebOrganizer's TopicClassifier on our FineWeb-Edu/DCLM-Edu shards and upweight Software Development / Software / Hardware / Science & Technology and the Tutorial / Documentation / Q&A Forum formats.

Mixing by topic and format adds to quality filtering instead of repeating it. WebOrganizer: FineWeb-Edu-filtered data with a Topic x Format reweighting rose from 54.2 to 56.2 average (1B models). OLMo 3 / Dolma 3 builds its web mix from WebOrganizer topic x quality buckets (secondary sources).

Facts in varied wordings: Nemotron-CC's synthetic rephrasings (Diverse QA, Distill, Knowledge List) of its high-quality pages beat plain repetition (average 56.7 vs 55.8 when synthetic replaced 4 of 8 repetitions), and Nemotron-CC-HQ reached MMLU 59.0 vs DCLM 53.4 vs FineWeb-Edu 42.9 at 8B/1T. The scale differs from ours and some of the gain is MMLU-shaped QA, so treat it as a modest (3-6%) ingredient, not a replacement for FineWeb-Edu. All synthetic text (Nemotron, Cosmopedia) is model-written and can carry made-up facts, which matters because the owner cares about made-up answers. Cap synthetic text so that real text (FineWeb-Edu, DCLM-Edu, Wikipedia, books) stays the majority.

Cosmopedia v2 at 15% is on the high side compared with published small-model use: SmolLM2-1.7B used 4% in its decay, and the 135M/360M shares are unconfirmed. Its 28B tokens cover 15% (12B pieces) in under one pass, but its single-generator style (Mixtral) lowers variety. 8-12% is a safer default, filtered toward college-level and CS/maths/science topics. Middle-school-audience textbooks scored best on everything except MMLU.

Ultra-FineWeb is a small step over FineWeb-Edu (+1.3 average, MMLU 32.24 vs 31.80 at 1B/100B) from the same FineWeb source. It can replace part of the FineWeb-Edu share, but don't add it on top without dedup between them.

Licence watch: FineWeb-Edu, SmolLM-Corpus, Essential-Web and FinePDFs are ODC-By. DCLM and DCLM-Edu are CC-BY-4.0, and the DCLM card notes research intent. Nemotron-CC v1 is under Common Crawl terms, while v2 is gated under NVIDIA's training-only agreement and may pass on Qwen/DeepSeek terms. The WebOrganizer licence is unconfirmed. The owner should accept any gated terms himself.

Long-context phase: SmolLM3 reached good results up to 64k by training on its decay mix at longer lengths with a higher RoPE theta. Upsampling long books/repos/web pages gave no extra RULER/HELMET gains. So the 16,384 phase need not be all long documents; keep the decay mix and add natural long documents (FinePDFs-Edu, books, code files) for the needle tests.

Unconfirmed and to measure on the server, not guess: the token size of FineWeb-Edu int_score >= 4 (sum token_count), DCLM-Edu token count, Cosmopedia per-topic sizes, and the ratio between our 16k pieces and GPT-2 tokens (the expected ~1.1x is an estimate).

datasets.name: Stack-Edu (educational code, 15 languages)
datasets.size: About 125B tokens in total, 167,063,359 rows, 17.5 GB of metadata parquet (the code itself is not stored on HF). Per-language tokens from the HF subset list, tokenizer not clearly named on the card (probably the SmolLM2 49k tokenizer, unconfirmed): Java 42.1B (45M rows, threshold 2), Python 21.8B (25.3M), C++ 16.0B (16.2M), Markdown 14.0B (20.7M), C 11.1B (5.85M), JavaScript 11.1B (13.3M), SQL 9.62B (2.5M), PHP 9.07B (9.91M), C# 8.87B (11.4M), Shell 3.13B (4.13M), TypeScript 3.03B (4.29M), Swift 1.83B, Go 1.80B (1.92M), Rust 1.75B (1.14M), Ruby 1.61B. No HTML/CSS subset. With our 16k vocabulary, code will probably take roughly 15-30% more pieces than these counts (estimate, not measured).
datasets.licence: No single dataset licence. The card says to see The Stack v2. Each file keeps its own licence: rows carry license_type 'permissive' or 'no_license'. Code use must follow each file's original licence, including attribution. Getting the file contents means downloading from the Software Heritage S3 bucket (softwareheritage/content/{blob_id}) with your own AWS credentials. The card says this takes about 6 hours on a 16-core us-east-1 machine. The Stack v2 terms say bulk downloads need an agreement with Software Heritage/INRIA (datasets@softwareheritage.org), and training must follow the Software Heritage principles for LLM training. Opt-out runs through 'Am I in the Stack' and the bigcode opt-out-v2 repo, and users must keep their copy current as removal requests are applied.
datasets.quality_notes: Made from the 15 largest StarCoder2Data languages (about 450B tokens). 15 per-language StarEncoder classifiers were trained on Llama3-70B-Instruct scores (0-5). Threshold 3 was used for every language except Java (2). SmolLM2 ablations, MultiPL-E unfiltered to filtered: Python 20.7 to 25.6, C++ 16.7 to 24.8, JavaScript 18.2 to 22.4, Java 17.6 to 22.7. This is the strongest open code source for small models. Watch out for 'no_license' files if licence purity matters.
datasets.recommended_subset: Main code source. About 9.6B pieces (12% of 80B) needs under 1 pass, so no repetition. Suggested weights within code: Python about 35%; JavaScript and TypeScript 12% together; Java 8% (downsample, it is the biggest and least useful for an all-rounder); C and C++ 12%; C# 5%; SQL 5%; Shell 4%; Go and Rust 3% each (their whole subsets, 1 pass); PHP 3%; Markdown 5-8% (README and docs prose, good for 'computer knowledge'). Hold the highest-scoring slice (score 4+ where available) for the final decay phase. HTML/CSS have to come from The Stack v2 / StarCoder2Data with a filter.
datasets.used_by: SmolLM2-1.7B: Stack-Edu replaced StarCoderData in stage 3 (8-10T) and was 24% of the decay stage (10-11T). SmolLM2-135M/360M used it from the start, single stage (exact shares not published). SmolLM3: added in stage 2 (8-10T, code 15%), and code was 24% in decay (10-11.1T).
datasets.version_date: 2025 (SmolLM2 paper published 4 Feb 2025). No update date on the card. Source graph: Software Heritage 2023-09-06.

datasets.name: The Stack v2 / StarCoder2Data (train-smol-ids, train-full-ids)
datasets.size: The Stack v2 in full: 3B+ files, 600+ languages, about 67.5 TB uncompressed (32.1 TB deduplicated). The train-full set is about 900B tokens (StarCoder2 tokenizer, per the StarCoder2 paper). Token count for train-smol: unconfirmed. The card says '17 languages' but lists 39 entries, including Markdown, JSON, YAML and Dockerfile.
datasets.licence: 'other', gated. Same Software Heritage terms as Stack-Edu: files are permissive or no-licence, original licences and attribution must be followed, bulk content needs a SWH/INRIA agreement, contents are fetched from S3 by blob_id, and opt-out removals must be honoured. Latest version v2.2.0 removed repos opted out before 2026-07-29.
datasets.quality_notes: Heuristic filtering only, so lower quality than Stack-Edu. Useful for languages Stack-Edu lacks (HTML, CSS, notebooks, config files) and for whole-repository grouping (long code files for the 16k phase).
datasets.recommended_subset: Small top-up only: HTML/CSS and Dockerfile/YAML/JSON about 0.5-1B pieces in total, after an educational-style classifier or heuristic filter. Repo-grouped long files are a source for the 16,384-window phase.
datasets.used_by: StarCoder2 (3.3-4.3T tokens). SmolLM2 stage 3 used StarCoder2Data subsets for languages with under 4B tokens in Stack-Edu. SmolLM3 stage 1 code (12%) was The Stack v2 plus PRs, notebooks and issues.

datasets.name: Kaggle notebooks + GitHub issues (issues-kaggle-notebooks)
datasets.size: Kaggle: about 580k notebooks, about 1.7B tokens. GitHub issues: about 15.5M rows, about 11B tokens. 18.6 GB in total. The tokenizer is not stated.
datasets.licence: No overall licence stated. The Kaggle part comes from Meta Kaggle Code (Apache 2.0). Licence for the issues part: unconfirmed.
datasets.quality_notes: The notebooks are rendered as Markdown with the title and dataset description, plus code and cell outputs (for example df.info() results). That makes them good 'code with explanation and results' text, mainly data science in Python. The issues are noisy conversational technical text. Filter them for length and quality and remove bot comments.
datasets.recommended_subset: Kaggle notebooks in full, about 1.7B tokens, 1-2 passes (about 2-3B pieces). GitHub issues: at most about 0.5-1B pieces of a quality-filtered slice, or count them in the CS-knowledge family instead.
datasets.used_by: SmolLM3 stage 1 code mix (Jupyter/Kaggle notebooks, GitHub issues). SmolLM2 stage 3 added Jupyter notebooks from StarCoder2 (size not given).
datasets.version_date: 2024 (cites StarCoder2 paper of 29 Feb 2024). No card date.

datasets.name: StarCoder2Data extras (documentation, Stack Overflow, lhq, Kaggle scripts)
datasets.size: Rows only: documentation 59.7k, stackoverflow 10.4M, issues 15.5M, kaggle 580k (as scripts), lhq 7.04M (APPS, CodeContests, GSM8K-style high-quality code), owm 6.32M, arxiv 1.56M, wikipedia 6.63M, plus IR subsets. 151 GB in total. Token counts are not on the page (unconfirmed). The Jupyter-structured split described in the paper was not released, because it needs a SWH agreement.
datasets.licence: Not stated on the page (unconfirmed). Stack Overflow content is CC-BY-SA in its source.
datasets.quality_notes: The library documentation and lhq subsets are high-value code-with-explanation text. Stack Overflow overlaps with the CS-knowledge family.
datasets.recommended_subset: documentation (all) and lhq (all) for code. Leave stackoverflow to the CS-knowledge family to avoid double counting.

datasets.name: Python-Edu (SmolLM-Corpus)
datasets.size: 7.68M rows. Token count not on the card. 'About 4B tokens' appears only in secondary sources (unconfirmed).
datasets.licence: The corpus is ODC-By. For the code contents the card points to The Stack v2 terms, and files are downloaded from the SWH S3 bucket.
datasets.quality_notes: Python files scored 4+ by the educational code classifier (stricter than Stack-Edu's 3). Largely covered by Stack-Edu Python.
datasets.recommended_subset: Use only as the top-quality Python slice in the decay phase, or skip it and take score-4+ files from Stack-Edu Python.

datasets.name: OpenCoder annealing corpus
datasets.size: algorithmic_corpus 5.32M rows, synthetic_code_snippet 3.08M rows, synthetic_qa about 7.17M rows. 26.8 GB in total. Tokens unconfirmed.
datasets.licence: ODC-By (dataset). The generating model is not stated.
datasets.quality_notes: Algorithm-focused code from The Stack v2, plus synthetic snippets and Q&A rewritten from it. Built as annealing data. This is the closest open thing to 'synthetic code textbooks with explanations'.
datasets.recommended_subset: synthetic_qa and synthetic_code_snippet in the decay phase, about 1-1.5B pieces.
datasets.used_by: OpenCoder (annealing phase; share not stated on the card).

datasets.name: Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v1 (synthetic code Q&A)
datasets.size: Synthetic code Q&A 174.9B tokens in 11 programming languages. Metadata to rebuild 747.4B tokens of curated GitHub code. Tokenizer not specified.
datasets.licence: NVIDIA Open Data License, gated, model training only. Synthetic parts come from Qwen and DeepSeek models, whose licence terms may pass on to trained models.
datasets.quality_notes: Large and filtered for correctness. The licence is more restrictive than ODC-By/Apache, so check it fits the project.
datasets.recommended_subset: Optional: about 1B pieces of the Python/JS Q&A in decay, only if the licence is acceptable.
datasets.used_by: NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 2 pretraining (share not checked).

datasets.name: FineMath (finemath-3plus, finemath-4plus, infiwebmath-3plus, infiwebmath-4plus)
datasets.size: finemath-3plus 34B tokens / 21.4M docs; finemath-4plus 9.6B tokens / 6.7M docs; infiwebmath-3plus 20.5B / 13.9M; infiwebmath-4plus 8.5B / 6.3M. The tokenizer is not named on the card (probably the SmolLM2 tokenizer, unconfirmed).
datasets.licence: ODC-By 1.0, plus Common Crawl terms of use.
datasets.quality_notes: Common Crawl pages from FineWeb URLs, re-extracted with maths/LaTeX kept, classified on 3- and 5-point scales by Llama-3.1-70B annotations, MinHash-deduplicated, English-only, and decontaminated against GSM8K, MATH and MMLU. FineMath-4+ gave about 2x GSM8K and 6x MATH compared with InfiMM-WebMath in 1.7B annealing ablations (60B maths tokens on a 3T checkpoint). InfiWebMath-4+ plateaued after about 80B tokens (repetition) and FineMath-4+ did not. A 50/50 mix of FineMath-3+ and InfiWebMath-3+ (about 50B) matched FineMath-3+. Deduplicating across the two hurt.
datasets.recommended_subset: Core maths web text. FineMath-4+: 2-3 passes (about 20-29B GPT-2-like, probably more pieces with our 16k vocab). Put about half in the stable phase and up-weight it in decay. FineMath-3+ and InfiWebMath-3+: fill the rest of the stable-phase maths. Do not deduplicate FineMath against InfiWebMath.
datasets.used_by: SmolLM2-1.7B: maths was about 10% in stage 3 (OWM plus InfiMM-WebMath) and 14% in decay (InfiWebMath-3+, FineMath-4+, small OWM and AugGSM8K). SmolLM2-135M/360M had FineMath from the start. SmolLM3: stage 1 maths 3% (FineMath-3+, InfiWebMath-3+), stage 2 10% (adds FineMath-4+, InfiWebMath-4+, MegaMath), decay 13%.
datasets.version_date: Dec 2024 release (described in the SmolLM2 paper, Feb 2025). No card date.

datasets.name: MegaMath
datasets.size: 371.6B tokens in total (tokenizer not stated). Web 263.9B (106.5M docs), Web-Pro 15.1B (15.0M), Code 28.1B (13.4M), synthetic 64.5B: translated code 7.2B, Q&A 7.0B, text-and-code blocks 50.3B.
datasets.licence: ODC-By
datasets.quality_notes: Re-extracted Common Crawl maths, maths-related Stack v2 code, and synthetic Q&A and interleaved text-and-code. Web-Pro is the refined top tier. In NVIDIA's 8B mid-training ablation, MegaMath-Web (not Pro) was a little below FineMath-3+ on MATH (31.6 vs 34.6) and GSM8K (78.24 vs 79.45).
datasets.recommended_subset: Web-Pro (15.1B) about 1 pass in the stable phase. Q&A (7.0B) and text-and-code blocks (subsample about 2B) for maths-with-code reasoning in decay. Skip the bulk Web part, because FineMath covers it at better quality.
datasets.used_by: SmolLM3 stage 2 maths (share within the 10% not given).

datasets.name: OpenWebMath
datasets.size: 14.7B tokens (tokenizer not stated on the card; the paper probably uses Llama, unconfirmed), 6,315,233 docs, 27.4 GB parquet.
datasets.licence: ODC-By 1.0, plus Common Crawl terms of use.
datasets.quality_notes: Older Common Crawl maths extraction (2013-2023). Weaker than FineMath in SmolLM2 ablations (OWM peaked about 10% GSM8K vs InfiMM 14%). Overlaps heavily with FineMath and Proof-Pile-2.
datasets.recommended_subset: Skip, or at most a small share (under 0.5B). FineMath supersedes it.
datasets.used_by: OLMo 2 pretraining (12.2B tokens, about 0.31% of 3.9T). SmolLM2 stages 2-4.

datasets.name: Proof-Pile-2 (arxiv, open-web-math, algebraic-stack)
datasets.size: arxiv 29B, open-web-math 15B, algebraic-stack 11B tokens (tokenizer not named on the card; the Llemma paper probably used Llama 2, unconfirmed). Versions v1.0.0 and v1.1.0.
datasets.licence: No single licence. The card says the underlying licences are unchanged (unconfirmed per subset).
datasets.quality_notes: algebraic-stack is maths code (Lean, Isabelle, Coq, numerical Python, Matlab and so on). arxiv is LaTeX papers: long, good for the 16k phase, and also useful for science.
datasets.recommended_subset: algebraic-stack about 1-2B pieces (filter to Python, SymPy, NumPy, Lean). Use arxiv as a 16k long-document source, shared with the science family. Skip its open-web-math copy (duplicate).
datasets.used_by: Llemma. OLMo 2 pretraining used Algebraic-Stack 11.8B and arXiv 20.8B (0.30% and 0.53%).

datasets.name: Nemotron-CC-Math v1
datasets.size: 3plus 133B tokens / 101.15M docs; 4plus 52B / 45.10M; 4plus_MIND 73B / 88.73M. Tokenizer not stated.
datasets.licence: NVIDIA Open Data License, gated, model training only. Made with phi-4, so the Phi-4 licence may apply.
datasets.quality_notes: The best maths web data in published ablations. 8B mid-training, 3plus vs FineMath-3+: MATH 44.2 vs 34.6, GSM8K 80.06 vs 79.45, MMLU-STEM 64.26 vs 62.29, and it also helped code (MBPP+ 43.51 vs 29.19).
datasets.recommended_subset: If the licence is acceptable: 4plus as the main high-quality maths source (5-8B pieces, under 1 pass), in place of part of FineMath-3+. 4plus_MIND (maths rewritten as dialogues and varied wordings) about 1-2B in decay.

datasets.name: OpenMathInstruct-2
datasets.size: About 14M problem-solution pairs in train (about 22M rows across all splits), 12.6 GB. Splits train_1M, train_2M, train_5M (fair downsampled). Tokens not stated.
datasets.licence: CC-BY-4.0. Generated with Llama3.1-405B-Instruct (Llama 3.1 licence terms may also apply, unconfirmed).
datasets.quality_notes: Augmented from the GSM8K and MATH training sets: new problems plus chain-of-thought solutions. A contamination explorer was released. About 0.1% of questions are over 1024 Llama tokens, and the authors suggest removing them. The style is narrow, so too much of it makes pretraining text uniform.
datasets.recommended_subset: train_1M (or train_2M) in the decay phase, about 0.3-0.6B pieces. Filter out over-long items and keep the rest for the maths fine-tune.

datasets.name: NuminaMath-CoT
datasets.size: 859,594 rows, 1.23 GB. Sources: cn_k12 276,591; synthetic_math 167,895; orca_math 153,334; olympiads 150,581; synthetic_amc 62,111; aops_forum 30,201; math 7,478; gsm8k 7,345; amc_aime 4,072.
datasets.licence: Apache-2.0
datasets.quality_notes: Competition-heavy chain-of-thought. Harder than a 560M model can mostly use. Includes an Orca-Math share (overlaps with Orca-Math).

datasets.name: Dolmino-mix-1124 maths (OLMo 2 mid-training maths)
datasets.size: Maths subsets (tokenizer not stated; OLMo 2 uses a cl100k-based tokenizer, unconfirmed on the card): TinyGSM-MIND 6.48B, MathCoder2 3.87B, TuluMath 230M, Metamath-owmfilter 84.2M, DolminoSynthMath 28.7M, GSM8K 2.74M, CodeSearchNet-owmfilter 1.78M. About 10.7B in total.

datasets.quality_notes: Maths was 20.8% of the 50B mid-training mix, 17.5% of 100B, and 10.8% of 300B, repeated up to 4x in the 300B mix. The Dolmino mid-training mix has no raw code except StackExchange (2.45%).
datasets.recommended_subset: TinyGSM-MIND and MathCoder2 as decay maths, about 1-2B pieces together.

lessons: Code share in strong small models rises over the run. SmolLM2-1.7B: 10% (StarCoderData) in stage 1, 20% in stage 2, then Stack-Edu from stage 3, and 24% in the decay stage. SmolLM3: 12%, then 15%, then 24% in decay. For our 80B single run, 12% code in the stable phase is in line with these, and code could rise to about 20% in the final 10-20% decay.

Maths share also rises late. SmolLM2-1.7B: 0% in stage 1, 5% in stage 2, about 10% in stage 3, 14% in decay. SmolLM3: 3%, then 10%, then 13%. OLMo 2 pretraining had only about 0.6% maths (OpenWebMath and Algebraic-Stack) but 10.8-20.8% maths in mid-training. Draft suggestion: maths about 8% in the stable phase and about 15% in decay, which averages about 10%.

Small models trained on a short budget did not use stages. SmolLM2-135M/360M (2T and 4T tokens) put Stack-Edu, FineMath, InfiMM-WebMath and Cosmopedia in the single mix from the start, with WSD decay over the last 20%. For 80B tokens, one stable mix plus a decay mix weighted toward the best code and maths is the closest proven recipe.

Keep the best data for the decay. SmolLM2 kept FineMath-4+ and its highest-quality code for the decay phase 'to maximize their impact', and SmolLM3 added OpenMathReasoning only in decay. OLMo 2's mid-training was mostly synthetic maths (TinyGSM-MIND, MathCoder2).

Educational filtering is worth more than volume for code. Stack-Edu's threshold-3 classifier raised MultiPL-E Python from 20.7 to 25.6 and C++ from 16.7 to 24.8. Java worked best at threshold 2. At 9.6B pieces of code we need under 1 pass of Stack-Edu (125B), so filtering harder (score 4 for Python and JS) costs nothing.

Maths web text: FineMath-4+ was far better than InfiMM-WebMath (about 2x GSM8K, 6x MATH at 1.7B) and did not plateau with repetition, while InfiWebMath-4+ plateaued after about 80B tokens. Do not deduplicate FineMath against InfiWebMath: HF found that it hurt. Nemotron-CC-Math-3+ beat FineMath-3+ on MATH (44.2 vs 34.6, 8B model), but its licence is training-only, NVIDIA terms.

Repetition: SmolLM2 kept most sets near 4-5 passes. FineMath-4+ (9.6B) can take 2-3 passes. Orca-Math, MetaMathQA and NuminaMath are tiny (under 1 GB) and can take about 4 passes in decay without hitting the Muennighoff limit.

Synthetic Q&A maths (OpenMathInstruct-2, MetaMathQA, Orca-Math, NuminaMath) has a narrow style and is mostly used for SFT. In pretraining, keep it to a small decay share (about 1-2B pieces in total). MetaMathQA's rephrasings match the 'varied wordings' rule. Leave competition sets (olympiad, AMC/AIME) for a bigger model.

Notebooks rendered with Markdown and outputs (Kaggle, about 1.7B tokens, Apache 2.0) give code with explanation and results. Both SmolLM2 (stage 3) and SmolLM3 (stage 1) used notebooks. StarCoder2's Jupyter-structured split was never released, because it needs a Software Heritage agreement.

Practical blocker: Stack-Edu, Python-Edu and The Stack v2 hold only IDs. The code must be pulled from the Software Heritage S3 bucket with our own AWS account (the card says about 6 hours on a 16-core us-east-1 machine). Bulk use formally needs a SWH/INRIA agreement, and opted-out repos must be dropped (v2.2.0 removed opt-outs to 2026-07-29). Plan this before renting the 8x B200.
Stack-Edu has no HTML/CSS, and Go (1.8B) and Rust (1.75B) are small. Take HTML/CSS from The Stack v2 with a filter, and treat Go and Rust as 1-pass whole subsets.

Long context: SmolLM2's 8k extension used 40% long documents (DCLM, FineWeb-Edu, Dolma books) and 60% of the decay mix. SmolLM3 found that extra long code repos and books did not improve RULER/HELMET beyond upsampling maths, code and reasoning. For our 2B-piece 16k phase, repo-grouped code files and arXiv LaTeX (Proof-Pile-2) are natural long code/maths sources, but they do not need a big share.

Token counts on these cards use various tokenizers (often unnamed: SmolLM2 49k, StarCoder2, Llama, cl100k). With our 16,384-piece vocabulary, code and LaTeX will likely take noticeably more pieces than the published counts. Measure it on a sample before fixing shares.

lessons: These sources are big enough to fill the 6% CS share (about 4.8B pieces of 80B) in one pass: the Stack Exchange tech sites (whole network 23.9B Comma tokens / 89.7 GB; Stack Overflow alone 10.26B StarCoder2 tokens), OpenCoder's code-related FineWeb pages (148 GB), the CS part of Cosmopedia v2 (28B total), and FinePDFs-Edu CS documents (90.8B English total). These are small but high value and worth 3-4 passes: OpenStax Intro to CS, PEPs, Python docs, MDN, ArchWiki, tldr-pages, the CS shelves of LibreTexts and PressBooks, OLMo 2's filtered Stack Exchange (1.26B tokens), and cs.* arXiv abstracts. All of the docs and textbooks together are well under 1B pieces.

Suggested split of the 4.8B (my proposal, not from a report): vote-filtered Stack Exchange tech sites 2.4B (one pass); OpenCoder web pages filtered to FineWeb-Edu score >= 3, about 1.0B; docs and open textbooks about 0.2B unique x 3-4 = 0.7B; cs.* arXiv abstracts about 0.25B x 2 = 0.5B (unless already in the science 2%); the remaining ~0.2B from the StarCoder2 documentation crawl or Cosmopedia v1 stanford/wikihow CS rows. Weight Cosmopedia v2 computer topics and Wikipedia computing articles up inside their own shares rather than counting them twice.

Comma v0.1 (Common Pile, 2025) repeated its small high-quality sources 6 times (Stack Exchange 23.9B x 6 = 143B effective, about 14% of 1T). It was strong on MMLU, ARC and code, but weak on HellaSwag and PIQA because it lacked everyday web text. Keep FineWeb-Edu as the base, and do not go past about 4 passes here (Muennighoff).

OLMo 2 put a small, already-filtered Stack Exchange set (1.26B tokens) at about 2.5% of its 50B and 100B mid-training (annealing) mixes, and DeepSeek-Coder trained on 87% code plus 10% code-related English (GitHub Markdown and Stack Exchange; from memory of the paper, not re-checked). So use the best-voted Stack Exchange and the docs in the final stretch, and pair code with prose about code.

SmolLM3 put Stack Exchange inside its 12% code share in stage 1, added Stack-Edu in stage 2, and raised high-quality code to 24% in the final stage. StarCoder2 used Stack Overflow (10.26B) and a 1.6B documentation crawl at all model sizes, 3B included.

Filtering by quality pays off at small size. Python-Edu kept 4B of 40B tokens (edu classifier score >= 4) and converged more than 3x faster. YuLan kept Stack Exchange answers with score >= 4 and preferred accepted answers. HF H4 gives each answer a pm_score = round(log2(1+upvotes)) +1 if accepted. Common Pile's Stack Exchange has no vote filter at all (only language and PII), so filter it yourself.

Format Stack Exchange as the question, then the accepted answer, then at most 2 more by votes, with no comments. It gives the same fact in several wordings (good for remembering facts) and looks like Q&A, but it is not assistant chat, so it does not count toward the 5% conversation limit. Its curt forum tone ('possible duplicate', 'what have you tried') is not a style the assistant should learn: drop very short answers and comment-like replies.

Licence warning: since July 2024 the official Stack Exchange dump requires the downloader to tick a box promising not to train LLMs on it (critics, including Archive Team, say this conflicts with CC BY-SA). Common Pile used Internet Archive community dumps from December 2024; RedPajama and TxT360 used older dumps. All copies are ShareAlike with attribution required. The owner should choose the copy knowingly.

Watch for non-commercial licences. MIT OCW (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) explicitly bans commercial AI-training use. Think Python 3e and OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, even though some catalogues list the OpenStax book as CC BY. OpenStax Introduction to Computer Science is CC BY 4.0 and safe. Open Data Structures is CC BY only in the author's own edition.

Everyday computer basics (files, operating systems, the internet, networking, hardware, staying safe online) has no clean open dataset. The best sources are ArchWiki, tldr-pages, MDN (how the web works), Super User / Ask Ubuntu / Unix & Linux / Security answers, Cosmopedia wikihow-style rows, and OpenCoder's FineWeb pages. FineWeb-Edu already contains much of this, so remove overlap before weighting up.

For the 16,384-window long phase, the CS candidates are whole open textbooks (OpenStax, LibreTexts CS, DOAB/PressBooks CS books), openly licensed cs.* arXiv papers (Common Pile arxiv_papers), long FinePDFs-Edu CS documents, and long ArchWiki and Python-docs pages.

Token counts in the reports use 49k-100k tokenizers (Comma, StarCoder2, LLaMA). With the 16,384-piece vocabulary the same text becomes more pieces; my rough rule is GB / 4 for prose and fewer bytes per piece for code-heavy Stack Overflow. Measure on a sample with the real tokenizer before fixing pass counts.
Keep the test questions' words out of all of these sources (the test_words rule), especially tldr, Stack Exchange and docs, which overlap with typical computer-basics test questions.

lessons: Supply is not the constraint. Wikipedia+Simple at 7% of 80B is about 5.6B pieces, about 1-1.3 passes over FineWiki (est. 4-5B pieces); Simple can be read up to about 4 times. Books at 5% (4B) fit inside Gutenberg 5.7B + DOAB 3.0B (Comma tokens) at under 1 pass. Science abstracts at 2% (1.6B) fit in peS2o s2ag (5.9B words) + arXiv abstracts. Non-tech Stack Exchange at 3% (2.4B) is likely enough once Stack Overflow and Maths SE are removed, but the non-tech size is unconfirmed. Count tokens on a sample with the 16k BPE before fixing shares.

Comma v0.1 (Common Pile, 2025) set its mix from small per-source test models and up-weighted sources that scored well. Strong sources were read up to 6 times (peS2o, Stack Exchange, Wikimedia, arXiv, DOAB); PubMed and old books x1; Library of Congress x0.25. Automatic mixing (MixMin) did not beat this hand-set mix. Its finish used only high-quality sources (DOAB up 2x; Gutenberg, PubMed and Pre-1929 dropped). Its science-heavy mix gave strong MMLU/ARC but weak HellaSwag/PIQA (no hobby, tutorial or blog text). For an all-rounder, keep everyday web text (FineWeb-Edu) large and do not let papers dominate.

Old public-domain books carry 19th-century English. Use Gutenberg mostly for the long phase and keep it about 3-5% in the main run, with modern DOAB books beside it. Skip OCR-heavy sets (Pre-1929, Library of Congress, Common Corpus OpenCulture) unless more long text is needed.

Licence checks for the owner. Institutional Books is noncommercial-only, no redistribution, and gated; leave it out unless the owner accepts those terms. Since 2024, Stack Exchange's download agreement asks users not to train LLMs on its dumps, which critics say conflicts with CC BY-SA. Common Pile's December 2024 copy is still marked CC BY-SA per document, but the owner should decide; pre-2024 copies (RedPajama, TxT360 Q4 2023) are an alternative. RedPajama's arXiv includes papers that are not CC-licensed, so prefer Common Pile's CC-only arXiv. PG-19 is Apache 2.0.

Varied wordings of facts: pair FineWiki (full articles) with Simple Wikipedia (the same facts, plainer), and let Cosmopedia and textbooks restate them. Optionally write infobox facts as a short sentence line. One wording repeated many times teaches the wording, not the fact.

Long-phase share across small and strong models. SmolLM2 (1.7B) went 2k to 8k over the final 75B of 11T tokens (about 0.7%), starting from a checkpoint before its decay, with RoPE base 130k and 40% long documents of at least 8k tokens (20% Dolma books, 10% DCLM, 10% FineWeb-Edu) plus 60% of the normal finishing mix. SmolLM3 went 4k to 32k (theta 1.5M) to 64k (theta 5M), 50B tokens each. Qwen2.5 went 4,096 to 32,768 in the final stage with RoPE base 10,000 to 1,000,000 (ABF). Qwen3 used the same base change, with reportedly 75% of the data at 16k-32k tokens and 25% at 4k-16k (secondary sources). Llama 3 405B used about 800B tokens (about 5% of 15.6T) in six steps from 8K to 128K, checking short benchmarks and needle tests at each step. The plan's 2B of 80B (2.5%) for a 4x step (4k to 16k) is in line: Fu et al. (2024) found 0.5-5B tokens of continued training enough for retrieval anywhere in 128K.

RoPE base for 16,384. Men et al. (2024) derive a minimum base of 3.1e5 for 16K (2.7e4 for 4K, 8.4e4 for 8K, 6.4e5 for 32K) and say the bound is not strict. Raise the base to about 1,000,000 at the start of the 16k phase (Qwen-style ABF), or 5e5 as a floor. The base 10,000 used in the 4k main run is below the 4K bound of 2.7e4; consider about 50k-100k from step 1 (a cheap change; untested here).

What the long data should be (ProLong, Gao et al. 2024, 40B tokens on Llama-3-8B). Code repositories and books are the best long sources, but only mixed with high-quality short data. Best average: about 60% long / 40% short. Final mix: 30% code repos, 30% books, 3% textbooks, 37% short (FineWeb-Edu 27%, FineWeb 27%, Wikipedia 11%, Stack Exchange 11%, Tulu 8%, OpenWebMath 8%, arXiv 8%). 100% long data hurts both long and short ability. Mask attention across document boundaries (it helped both long and short). PG-19 perplexity kept improving while real long-context skill got worse, so judge with retrieval tests, not perplexity. Training longer than the test length helped. Synthetic long instruction data hurt fine-tuning even at 1%.

Counterpoints. Fu et al. (2024): simply upsampling one domain such as books gives worse results; keep the domain balance of the main mix and pick the long documents within each domain. SmolLM3: upsampling extra long data (code repos, books, long web pages) beyond what was naturally long in its mix did not improve RULER/HELMET. OLMo 3 used long olmOCR science PDFs plus synthetic long tasks (for example word extraction) for its 8K to 65K phase with YaRN, and reportedly about 1 part long to 2 parts short (one secondary source).

Proposed 16k phase for SlingerGPT 560M (about 2B pieces, inside the final learning-rate decay, not after it). About 60% long documents (12k-16k+ pieces, packed one per window where possible): about 25% books (Gutenberg + DOAB), 15% papers (CC arXiv, long peS2o s2orc, a little PMC), 15% concatenated code repos, 5% long FineWiki/FineWeb-Edu articles. About 40% short replay of the high-quality finishing mix. RoPE base raised to about 1M at the switch; cross-document attention masking. Check with held-out PG-19 test books (wrongness by position), a needle test, and the normal short tests, since the short tests must not drop. Supply: about 1.2B long pieces needed, under 1 pass of Gutenberg alone.

Science split suggestion: keep 'science abstracts' about 2% (peS2o s2ag + arXiv abstracts: dense, many topics) and add about 1% of CC arXiv/peS2o full text (CS, physics, maths, biology) for worked derivations and long structure. PubMed full text gets little or none in the main run; PubMed abstracts are covered by s2ag.

lessons: PRETRAINING SHARE, what strong models did. SmolLM2 put no chat or instruction data in pretraining: its stage-4 decay was web 58%, Stack-Edu 24%, maths 14%, Cosmopedia v2 4%. SmolLM3's decay stage (config stage3_9T_11T.yaml) has no SmolTalk or chat; instruction and reasoning sets total about 1.9% (OpenMathInstruct-2 0.5%, OpenMathReasoning 0.5%, OLMo problem-solving 0.3%, OLMo 2students 0.3%, natural_reasoning 0.1%, OpenCodeReasoning 0.05%). OLMo 2's 50B Dolmino anneal gave FLAN 16.6% (about 8.3B tokens) plus about 21% maths, much of it Q&A. In OLMo 2's ablation, web + instructions raised GSM* from 28.5 to 46.0 with MMLU flat; web + maths + instructions was best overall.

PRETRAINING SHARE, evidence that it helps. MiniCPM 2.4B mixed SFT data into the decay: MMLU 44.6 to 50.9, GSM8K 27.7 to 42.3, MBPP 24.4 to 30.3 against a plain decay plus the same 4B-token SFT. At 1.2B, decay with SFT data plus 6B tokens of SFT beat a plain decay plus 12B tokens of SFT on most tests. Instruction Pre-Training trained a 500M from scratch on 100B tokens with 1/5 of the texts turned into instruction-response pairs (about 10B tokens): ARC-e 50.3 to 54.8, BoolQ 57.5 to 62.0, PIQA down 71.1 to 69.9, and it gained more from later instruction tuning.

PRETRAINING SHARE, recommendation for the 80B run (judgement, not measured). About 3-4% conversation and instruction data in all, about 2.4-3.2B pieces. Keep it low (about 1-2%) in the main run and raise it to about 8-10% in the final decay (the last 10-15B pieces), in exactly the fine-tune's chat format. Spread it over several sources (SmolTalk all, UltraChat 200k, SODA, the English GPT-4 part of WildChat, OpenCoder realuser, the maths sets) so no source is read more than about 4 times. Count tokens with the 16k tokenizer first: no source above gives its size in the project's pieces. Keep canned refusals and 'The text doesn't say.' out of pretraining entirely.

FINE-TUNE RECIPES. SmolLM2-1.7B: SFT on SmolTalk (1.1M) for 2 epochs, LR 3e-4, batch 128, sequence 8,192; then DPO on UltraFeedback for 2 epochs, LR 1e-6, beta 0.5, length 1,024. SmolLM2-135M/360M: smol-smoltalk (about 460k) for 2 epochs at LR 1e-3 (config), cosine, warmup 10%, length 8,192, then the same DPO. SmolLM3-3B: 140B tokens of reasoning mid-training, then 1.8B-token SFT for 4 epochs (blog; the handbook yaml says 5) at LR 2e-5 with packing and user turns masked, then APO-zero (beta 0.05, LR 1e-6, 1 epoch). Tulu 3 8B: SFT 939k for 2 epochs (more did not help), LR 5e-6, batch 128, max 4,096, sum loss; then length-normalised DPO, beta 5, LR 5e-7, 1 epoch. Qwen2.5: SFT on over 1M examples for 2 epochs at 32k length, LR 7e-6 down to 7e-7; DPO on about 150k pairs for 1 epoch at LR 7e-7; then GRPO. Qwen3 0.6B-14B: no RL of their own but strong-to-weak distillation from Qwen3-32B or 235B (off-policy, then on-policy logit KL), about 1/10 of RL's GPU hours. Their LRs were tuned for AdamW; with Muon they must be re-found in a short sweep.

SIZE FOR A 560M (judgement). Something between smol-smoltalk (460k chats, used for 135M/360M) and SmolTalk (1.1M, used for 1.7B): about 600k-900k conversations, 1-2 epochs. Keep the project's 8% plain-text replay and copies at several steps: Tulu 3 and SmolLM2 both stop at about 2 epochs, and the project's maths peaked at 75% of the run.

CHAT FORMAT. SmolLM2 and Qwen2.5 use ChatML (<|im_start|>role\n...<|im_end|>) with a default system line naming the model ('You are a helpful AI assistant named SmolLM, trained by Hugging Face'). OLMo 2 1B uses <|user|> / <|assistant|> with <|endoftext|> after each assistant turn and no BOS. SmolLM3 and Qwen3 add /think and /no_think flags. Reserve 2-3 special pieces in the 16k vocabulary for turn start and end, so every reply ends on its own end piece. This also fixes the project's 'greetings never stop' failure without relying on marking the next 'User:' line.

PREFERENCE TUNING, measured at small size. OLMo 2 1B, SFT to DPO: IFEval 50.5 to 67.1, AlpacaEval2-LC 2.4 to 9.5, GSM8K 52.1 to 59.0, MMLU 36.4 to 39.9, safety 93.2 to 89.9, PopQA 12.7 to 12.3. So DPO mostly improves instruction-following and style and does not add facts. SmolLM2 found UltraFeedback the most consistently helpful preference set. Tulu 3 found length-normalised DPO beat SimPO, plain DPO and PPO; on-policy pairs (the model's own answers) beat off-policy; more unique prompts help and repeated prompts do not. I found no confirmed SimPO or APO numbers below 1B. SmolLM3 found APO lowered long-context (RULER) scores; merging (0.9 x APO soup + 0.1 x long-context mid-training checkpoint) restored them up to 128k. A similar merge could protect the 560M's 16k skill after preference tuning.

'I DON'T KNOW' WITHOUT SPREADING. Gekhman et al. 2024: fine-tuning on facts the model does not know is learned slowly and then raises hallucination. Early stopping makes it roughly harmless; filtering unknowns out helps; MaybeKnown examples (sometimes right) teach best (69.9 against 60.1 for HighlyKnown only); relabelling unknowns 'I don't know' removed the overfitting (accuracy on answered questions 61.8 either way). Kang et al. 2024: on unfamiliar questions the model copies the kind of answer its unfamiliar training examples had. This is exactly why the project's 'I don't know' followed question shape: make the 'knows' and 'does not know' sides match in phrasing, length and type (sums, short facts, how and why, 'Tell me about').

'I DON'T KNOW', MEASURED METHODS. R-Tuning splits data by whether the base model's own answer matches the label. Its refusal carried over to other datasets (LLaMA-13B HaluEval-QA 80.36 against 75.73) but at only a 44% answer rate on ParaRel, and over-refusal was not measured. Alignment for Honesty samples 10 answers and counts a question known when at least 10% are right (tau 0.1), on 8,000 TriviaQA questions. Over-conservativeness was 9.9% (Absolute) to 15.9% (Multisample), with almost no loss of helpfulness (8.62 to 8.56). The project's likelihood split (at most 0.5 knows, at least 0.75 does not, middle dropped) agrees with this literature. Add CoCoNot's 379-prompt contrast set plus the project's sums and narrow facts as over-refusal checks.

READING PRACTICE. Use only answerable questions, rewritten into full natural answers: SQuAD 2.0's answerable part, NQ with long answers (lower-case search phrasing, which the project lacks), CoQA Wikipedia and literature, and QuAC with the CANNOTANSWER turns removed. For several search results at once: HotpotQA distractor (10 paragraphs, 2 relevant, CC BY-SA 4.0), TriviaQA rc (about 6 documents, licence 'unknown') and Glaive RAG-v1 (Apache 2.0, multi-document with citations). Search-R1 (RL on NQ + HotpotQA) taught Qwen2.5-3B to issue its own searches, about 20% better than plain RAG, but the gain was much smaller than at 7B. For a 560M, supervised examples of 'search(query) -> results -> answer' are the safer first step (judgement).

LONG CONTEXT (16k). ProLong found SFT on short instructions only (UltraChat, 1B tokens) gave strong long-context results, and even 1% synthetic long instruction data hurt. Its long continued-pretraining mix was 30% code repositories, 30% books, 3% textbooks and 37% short data (FineWeb-Edu, FineWeb, Wikipedia, StackExchange, Tulu-v2 8% of the short part, OpenWebMath, arXiv). SmolLM3: extra long data beyond the natural long samples did not improve RULER or HELMET. So put the 16k skill mainly in the 2B-piece long phase (books, code files, papers) with about 35-40% short data mixed in. Keep long SFT small: a few thousand LongAlign examples cut to 16k, Qasper, QuALITY and NarrativeQA windows, plus the planned find-the-detail test. Check that short-chat quality does not drop.

MULTI-TURN AND TOPIC CHANGE. No public set targets topic switching. smol-magpie-ultra (about 6 turns in SmolTalk2), Magpie-Pro-MT (2 turns), UltraChat, WildChat multi-turn and oasst2 trees give long chats. Keep the project's own 'mixed' chats (several unrelated chats in one, short and long replies), since the model copies the length and topic of earlier replies. Tulu 3's ablation (no WildChat: AlpacaEval 12.4 to 7.5) shows real user prompts matter for natural chat.
